speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your fatigue, weight loss, and jaundice, have you noticed any changes in your stool or urine color, such as pale stools or dark urine? Also, do you have any abdominal pain or a history of alcohol use or hepatitis?

text: The ultrasound showing an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder without stones, combined with your significant weight loss and jaundice, strongly suggests a malignant obstruction rather than simple gallstones. I will request a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to better visualize the pancreas and biliary tree. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis_With_Contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan rules out pancreatic cancer, but the ultrasound finding of an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder without stones (Courvoisier's sign) combined with your alcohol history is highly suspicious for alcoholic hepatitis or another liver pathology. Let's evaluate the severity of liver damage and check for cirrhosis. REQUEST TEST: FibroScan, Viral_Hepatitis_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal CT and FibroScan, the significantly elevated ALP and bilirubin with a distended gallbladder suggest a distal common bile duct obstruction that may have been missed. I will request an MRCP to visualize the biliary tree in greater detail. REQUEST TEST: MRCP
